page: Microsoft Azure D32nls_v6 is a virtual machine within the network-optimized, low-memory Dnlv6 family. It operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor using the x86_64 architecture and provides 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with two threads per core. The underlying hardware is an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, featuring a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1 data cache. The processor incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AMX tile and int8 extensions, and cryptographic acceleration through AES and SHA-NI.

The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This low-memory ratio targets operational profiles where processing execution outpaces memory consumption. The D32nls_v6 includes no onboard local storage, zero dedicated GPUs, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on network-attached remote storage for persistence. The absence of local NVMe eliminates ephemeral storage maintenance overhead, though disk-heavy pipelines must account for network storage bandwidth constraints.

Benchmark evaluations show strong compute and memory bandwidth capabilities. The platform achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2079.0 and a multi-core score of 16529.0, alongside uncached large-block read memory bandwidth reaching 202.93 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput measures at 46.21 GB/sec. In machine learning workloads, the CPU supports high prompt processing speeds on 135M and 7B models, while compression and synthetic integer stress tests maintain middle-tier metrics.

Given its 1:2 memory-to-core ratio and dedicated high-frequency cores, the D32nls_v6 offers a resource-efficient posture for workloads that require strong compute capacity without paying for unneeded memory capacity. Suitable deployment targets include high-traffic web serving, software build pipelines, CI/CD runners, batch transformation jobs, and lightweight CPU inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D32nls_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running up to 4.2 GHz. Equipped with 64.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a 260 MB L3 cache, the system does not include local storage or hardware accelerators, depending on remote storage options for persistent disks. Benchmark results indicate strong standing in Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations, high uncached read memory bandwidth at 202.93 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput of 46.21 GB/sec. The instance also exhibits strong prompt processing performance in small and medium language model inference. Due to its balanced compute-to-RAM density and absence of local disks, the D32nls_v6 is suited for compute-heavy tasks, continuous integration pipelines, web serving clusters, and batch processing workloads.
